events.title: Bay Street May Open Higher; Tech Stocks Likely To Decline
events.description: Canadian stocks are seen opening on a positive note Tuesday morning, tracking higher gold prices and on easing worries about inflation following a sharp drop in oil prices. Tech stocks may find the going a bit tough amid renewed uncertainty about returns on AI investments.

events.title: FTSE 100 Rises 0.65% As Oil Prices Fall On Russia Export Lift
events.description: UK stocks climbed for a third consecutive session Tuesday, with the FTSE 100 gaining 0.65% to 10,725.98. Easing oil prices and bond yields supported sentiment, while Brent crude fell 1.7% to $104.90 a barrel as Russia partially lifted diesel export restrictions.

events.title: Johnson & Johnson Q3 Profit Plunges, Lifts FY26 Outlook; Stock Drops
events.description: Drug major Johnson & Johnson on Tuesday reported sharply lower third-quarter profit on special charges, despite sales growth. Further, the firm raised its fiscal 2026 outlook again and announced a quarterly dividend. In pre-market activity, the shares were losing around 2.6 percent.

events.title: CAC 40 Pares Early Gains
events.description:
After a firm start, France's equity benchmark CAC 40 pared gains and hovered around the flat line about an hour past noon on Tuesday as investors turned a bit cautious, looking ahead to the earnings season.

Falling oil prices and lower bond yields contributed to the positive start this morning.

events.title: Indian Shares Rally As IT Stocks Surge On AI Selloff
events.description: Indian shares logged strong gains on Tuesday, with information technology stocks leading the surge as enthusiasm for artificial intelligence eased.

events.title: German Equities Climb Amid Oil Retreat; September CPI Rises To 3.3%
events.description: German stocks climbed to a third consecutive session of gains Tuesday as easing oil prices and bond yields boosted sentiment. The DAX gained 0.44%, while Brent crude fell 2% to $104.40 per barrel after Russia partially lifted diesel export restrictions. Germany's September inflation accelerated to 3.3% year-on-year, the highest since December 2023.

events.title: Gold Inches Higher As Oil, Dollar Retreat
events.description: Gold prices were modestly higher on Tuesday as oil prices eased and the dollar retreated from an 18-month high ahead of key U.S. inflation data due later in week, which could influence Federal Reserve expectations.

events.title: Oil Prices Decline Amid Russian Diesel Relief
events.description: Oil prices fell sharply on Tuesday as Russia partially lifted its diesel export restrictions, helping ease supply constraints in global fuel markets.

events.title: European Shares Rise As Oil Prices Ease On Russian Diesel Supply Deal
events.description: European shares edged higher on Tuesday as oil prices eased and investors reacted to a slew of earnings.

events.title: Asian Shares Mostly Lower Amid AI Jitters
events.description: Asian stocks retreated on Tuesday, with tech stocks coming under pressure as warnings mounted around the AI trade.

events.title: European Shares Poised For Cautious Open Amid AI Jitters
events.description: European stocks are seen opening broadly lower on Tuesday as investors await key U.S. inflation data and corporate earnings in the coming days for direction.

events.title: Australia Business Confidence Weakens For Third Straight Month: NAB
events.description: Australia's business sentiment deteriorated for the third straight month in September amid concerns about higher interest rates, global uncertainty and elevated fuel costs, monthly business survey results from the National Australia Bank showed Tuesday. The business sentiment index fell to -13 from -9 in August. At the same time, the business conditions index was unchanged at 1 point in September.

events.title: Indian Shares Sharply Higher As IT Stocks Surge On AI Slowdown Worries
events.description: Indian shares were sharply higher in early trade on Tuesday, with information stocks leading the surge as enthusiasm for artificial intelligence eased.
